Iban diphthongization: 'a process where final *-a(C) became -ay or -aw in a number of lexemes' (p. 193); a final consonant is lost with it. Smith found 25 cases of -ay, eight of them in all of Iban, Seberuang and Mualang, and eight of -aw, two of them in all three. In the Iban of the upper Kapuas it 'agrees with that reported in Adelaar (1992a) and Nothofer (1988), lexeme-by-lexeme' (p. 193); 13 of the 23 inconsistent cases are in Iban alone (p. 194).
examples: 'hold' məgay; 'road' jalay; 'come' datay; 'big' bəsay; 'long' pañay; 'old' tuay; 'eat' makay; 'fly' tərbay; 'mat' tikay; 'we incl' kitay; 'feel' asay; 'go home' pulay; 'shrimp' unay; 'plate' piŋay; 'flower' buŋay; 'derris' tubay; 'naked' təlañay
